caption: A simple shulker box unloader: a dispenser places a full box on a hopper that empties it, and when the box is empty a piston breaks it so it drops into a second hopper. Details: a comparator reads the box through a stone; a repeater squares it and feeds a subtract comparator twice (directly on its side, 4 ticks late on its rear), which gives a 4-tick pulse only when the box runs empty. The pulse fires a sticky piston that pushes a stone into the box cell; the moving stone pushes the drop into the walled drop cell over the empties hopper, and the same pulse locks the emptying hopper so it cannot pick the box up. An observer on the pushed stone fires the dispenser for the next box. Started by a lever.

The simple shulker box unloader judged with 16-stack items (snowballs): a dispenser places a full box on a hopper that empties it, and a piston breaks the empty box into a second hopper. Details: the same build as the 64-stack reference unloader.

The simple shulker box unloader judged with unstackable items (iron shovels): a dispenser places a full box on a hopper that empties it, and a piston breaks the empty box into a second hopper. Details: the same build as the 64-stack reference unloader.

A self-running shulker box loader that also sends off a half-full box when the items stop coming: a piston breaks the box when it is full or when its feeding hopper runs dry. Details: a comparator reads the feeding hopper, which is never empty while items flow (it pushes and pulls in the same tick); an observer watching that comparator pulses when the hopper runs empty, and through a stone and a repeater (delay 2: a 2-tick pulse would make the sticky piston spit its stone) it fires the piston, so the box leaves with whatever it holds when the input stops for good. The rest is the self-running loader.

A shulker box loader that runs by itself with no lever: a dispenser places an empty box, a hopper fills it, a piston breaks the full box into a hopper, and the dispenser starts again on its own whenever boxes come back. Details: a comparator reads the dispenser through the drop cell's roof, and an observer above that comparator fires the dispenser whenever it goes from holding no box to holding one, so it places the first box by itself and resumes after the box supply ran out. The rest is the reference loader: the full detector (a comparator in compare mode with a redstone block on its side, 15 only when full) fires a sticky piston two cells away that pushes a stone into the box.

A self-running shulker box loader that packs only one item kind (cobblestone) and passes everything else on to a reject chest. Details: the items go through a hopper item sorter: the filter hopper under the line holds 18 cobblestone and 4 named papers that never move, so it can only take cobblestone, which it pulls before the line hopper's 8-tick cooldown lets an item go on; a comparator on the filter hopper and a subtract comparator lock its output hopper until one more cobblestone arrives. The rest is the self-running loader.

Always-on shulker unloader, 2 hopper minecarts on an activator rail over 3 hoppers (track shulker-speed, clk-item). The dispenser D above the box cell X places full boxes. In the cell under X an activator rail runs east-west on top of the middle of three hoppers; two hopper minecarts stand still on it at the rail cell's two ends, each straddling two hoppers (a hopper pulls from every container entity whose box overlaps the cube above it) and each sucking X at 20 items/s, so the three hoppers drain X at 7.5 items/s into three item chests. The carts face 45 degrees so they never push each other. Empty detection as in the reference: comparator C reads X through a stone, repeater W squares it, subtract comparator V (side direct, rear 4 gt late through T) pulses when X becomes empty. The pulse powers, in the same tick, sticky piston P (its stone breaks the box and pushes the drop north into the walled drop cell over hopper K) and, through two dust under P, the activator rail, which disables both carts before they can suck the drop. Observer Q on the stone's cell re-fires D on the retraction. Comparator E reads D through the drop cell's roof and observer Q2 above it fires D whenever D's contents change: it places the first box by itself and again when boxes come back after the supply ran out.

Mixed-item shulker loader, the first with the mixed badge (track shulker-speed, clk-item): clk-rt's flush loader plus a jam detector. Comparator H reads the feeding hopper N; besides the flush observer G, H drives four dust whose power decays to L_N - 3, so the fourth dust is on only when N's level reaches 4 (a backlog: N's items stopped entering the box, which only happens when the box has no empty slot). Subtract comparator Vj turns its rising edge into a 4 gt pulse (its side gets the same signal 4 gt late through repeater Rs), and the pulse powers, through a dust and a stone, the sticky piston that breaks the box.

Shulker loader with both restart and flush (track shulker-speed, clk-item): clk-rt's always-on loader plus an hourglass flush that outlasts the restart pause. The hourglass is a chest Tc preloaded with 420 stone items (not a scenario item) over hopper Hd, which drains it into a sink chest only while the judge's items chest is empty AND the dispenser still holds boxes. Comparator CH reads the items chest and feeds repeater Rc. The dispenser comparator E drives repeater Y into a stone, and the wall torch on that stone is lit when the dispenser is empty. Both feed the dust line that locks Hd, through the floor under its last dust. Draining 420 items takes 3360 gt: longer than the restart pause (3000 gt) and within the flush deadline (6000 gt). It stays frozen once the dispenser is empty, so the spare box at the end of a normal run never starts it. When Tc runs empty, comparator HG turns off, and the wall torch on its output stone lights a dust line that powers the sticky piston through comparator Vj: the last partial box leaves, and the piston stays extended (the hourglass expires only once, at the end). Shrunk in the game from 75 blocks (an edge detector before the piston, and three floor stones, are not needed).

Two-station rail unloader (track shulker-speed, clk-item): two copies of shulker-speed-unloader-rail (copy B 6 blocks south of copy A) share one boxes chest through a hopper splitter, so two boxes empty in parallel. Splitter: hopper Hs under the boxes chest pushes north along a hopper line into copy A's box hopper; hopper U2 under Hs pulls from it and pushes south along a second line into copy B's box hopper. Boxes therefore alternate between the two dispensers. Each copy: two hopper minecarts on one activator rail under the box (one at each end of the rail cell) pull the box at 20 items/s and feed three hoppers (7.5/s); its comparator reads the box through a stone and fires the sticky piston when the box empties; the same pulse powers the activator rail so the carts do not swallow the broken box. Shrunk in the game from 122 blocks: the walls beside the box cells and the drop cells are not needed.

A one-block-wide unloader you can line up side by side with no gap: a dispenser drops each full box onto a hopper that empties it, and when the box is empty a piston breaks it into a second hopper that sends it on.  How it works (no redstone dust and no comparator side inputs, so neighbouring copies never touch each other's signals): - A comparator reads the emptying hopper. That hopper holds exactly 1 item while the box still has items, because it pushes and then pulls in the same tick. - When the hopper empties, the torch on the block the comparator powers (through a repeater) lights 3 gt later, and the sticky piston pushes a stone into the box cell. That is soon enough that the emptying hopper is still on its cooldown and cannot grab the box. The box's drop is pushed into the cell above the output hopper, which catches it at once. - An observer under the comparator toggles a copper bulb on every change of the comparator, so the bulb is lit while the box has items. While it is unlit, a torch under the block keeps the block powered, which ends the piston's pulse and holds it off until the next box's first item. Every comparator starts at 0, so the design is consistent as placed in any rotation. - An observer over the piston, watched by an observer on the dispenser, fires the dispenser after each break. A comparator reads the dispenser through a stone, and two observers watch it. When the dispenser gets its first box, they power the boxes hopper above it, which fires the dispenser by quasi-connectivity. That covers the start and refills after the supply ran out.

A shulker box loader you can line up side by side every 3 blocks: a hopper fills the box from above, a comparator watches it, and when it is full a piston breaks it into a hopper that sends it on, while a dispenser underneath places the next empty box. The 1-wide loader (shulker-loader-1wide) packs copies with no gap at 39 blocks; this one is smaller. Details: Here the feed hopper is above the box cell, the dispenser below it facing up, and the read on its east side: a comparator in compare mode with a redstone block on its side, 15 only when the box is full. That signal runs north along the third column through two repeaters and back west into the stone behind a sticky piston, whose stone breaks the box and pushes it into the drop cell over the output hopper. The dispenser fires whenever its contents change (a comparator reads it through a stone; two observers watch that comparator and power the stone under the dispenser), which places the first box and refills after a box shortage, and after every break (an observer under the first repeater of the full line, watched by an observer that powers the read-through stone).

A one-block-wide shulker unloader you can line up side by side with no gap (22 blocks): a dispenser drops each full box onto a hopper that empties it, and when the box is empty a piston pushes a block into it, which breaks it into a second hopper that sends it on. How it works: as the 24-block unloader (a comparator reads the emptying hopper, a copper bulb remembers whether the box still has items, a torch fires the piston when it is empty, an observer on the piston fires the dispenser after each break, a comparator reading the dispenser starts it), with the search's savings: the pushed block is an observer that fires the dispenser itself, a lamp and a bulb stand in as the solid blocks, a piston and an observer serve as supports. Found by `mctas circuit shulker anneal` (random edits, each judged on redsim with the judge's own scenarios) from the 24-block unloader: same box, same badges, same speed.

A one-block-wide shulker loader you can line up side by side with no gap (36 blocks, 1x6x11): a dispenser under the box spot places an empty box, the hopper above fills it from the items chest, and when the box is full a piston behind it breaks it; the dropped full box lands on the hopper under the box's front, which sends it to the output chest. How it works: a comparator reads the box and a copper bulb toggles once per full box; the comparator reading the bulb starts a chain of sticky pistons and observers over the top that ends at a dropper above the breaking piston, and the observer under that dropper fires the piston. A comparator on the first hopper of the box line (it sees a box arrive even one at a time, or from a chest kept full) and the observer next to the breaker both fire a dispenser block; a sticky piston then moves an observer down, and observers and droppers pass the pulse to a dropper under the box dispenser, which fires it without touching the hoppers beside it. It passes the judge's full-chest, endless-supply, one-box and one-box burst checks. Found by `mctas circuit shulker anneal --sweep 23,29,37` (every trickle phase required) from the 41-block 1x6x11 loader (pext).
